text: A web app's pipeline optimizes for shipping fast and rolling back fast. A deployed smart contract has none of that safety net — once bytecode is on-chain, there's no git revert for a contract holding user funds.

Because there's no fixing forward, the pipeline has to catch everything before the deploy transaction: correctness tests on every PR, static analysis, gas regressions, and human review gates before a deploy script runs.
None of this is optional the way it can feel optional on a web app, where a missed edge case ships a bug patched tomorrow. Here, a missed edge case can be the exploit.

A contract that compiles and passes every local test can still behave differently once deployed — real gas price, real block conditions, the real initial state of contracts it immediately interacts with.
One fact — immutability — reshapes the entire pipeline into a pre-deploy gate instead of a post-deploy safety net. Lesson 8 builds that gate for real, in GitHub Actions.
